title: Longest Common Subsequence: Two Bird-Watchers' Logs
summary: A grid of prefixes: a match extends the diagonal by one, a mismatch keeps the better of above and left.

analogy.scenario: Two bird-watchers each log species in the order they spot them, one letter per species: STONE and NOTES. What's the longest run of species both saw in the same order, not necessarily back to back?

mapping.real: A species code in a log
Species both saw in the same order
Comparing the first few entries of each log
mapping.abstract: Cell [i][j]: prefixes of length i and j

takeaway.pattern: Dynamic programming (2D table over two strings)
takeaway.summary: lcs[i][j] = diagonal + 1 when a[i − 1] = b[j − 1], else the larger of above and left. Fill row by row; the answer is the bottom-right cell.
takeaway.spaceComplexity: O(m × n), or O(n) keeping two rows
whenToUse: Answers over every pair of prefixes

scenes.narration: Two bird-watchers log species by letter: one wrote S, T, O, N, E, the other N, O, T, E, S. What's the longest run of species both saw in the same order?
scenes.caption: Two logs, STONE and NOTES: the longest shared order?

scenes.narration: Trying every subset of one log against the other grows exponentially. Instead, compare growing prefixes of both logs in a grid.
scenes.caption: Checking every subset of one log is exponential

scenes.narration: Each cell compares the first few entries of each log. With an empty log there's nothing in common: the top row and left column are 0.
scenes.caption: An empty log shares nothing: the edges are 0

scenes.narration: Fill row by row. S matches S at the end of the first row: both logs share it, so take the diagonal and add one.
scenes.caption: S meets S: the diagonal plus one

scenes.narration: T and E differ, so drop one of them: keep the larger of the cell above and the cell to the left. The 1 from the left carries over.
scenes.caption: T against E: no match, keep the better neighbor

scenes.narration: Near the end, E matches E, and the diagonal already holds a shared 1. One plus one: a shared run of 2.
scenes.caption: E meets E after a shared 1: the run grows to 2

scenes.narration: The last cell compares both whole logs. E and S differ, so it keeps the 2 from its left: the bottom-right cell holds the answer.
scenes.caption: The bottom-right cell covers both full logs: 2

scenes.narration: Species are characters and the logs are strings. Each cell needs only its three neighbors, so the table takes O(m times n) time.
scenes.caption: Species are characters; the logs are two strings
